data.title: Unit Test
data.tagline: A unit test tests one independently verifiable function, component, or small module.
data.learningOutcome: You can identify a small responsibility worth verifying alone and know when outside systems should stay out.
data.description: Pass a fixed price to a tax function and assert the amount, or check that a disabled button does not submit. It isolates outside services so a failure points to a small responsibility. A full login with browser, API, and real database is not a unit test.

learning.assumes: You have seen a function return a result from input.
learning.outcome: You can identify a small responsibility worth verifying alone and know when outside systems should stay out.

distinctions.label: Integration test
distinctions.explanation: A Unit Test isolates one function or component. An Integration Test checks whether modules or real dependencies cooperate correctly.

explanation.title: Check one small responsibility
explanation.text: Boundary inputs such as 100 gets 20 off and 99 gets none directly test the price rule. On failure, look at the calculation rather than guessing about network or database.

explanation.title: Keep outside dependencies controllable
explanation.text: Payment, network, or current time can be isolated or replaced when they make results slow or unstable. Unit tests are fast and precise, but do not prove systems work together.

data.boundary: A unit test is not a synonym for any small test or a full user journey. It verifies one relatively independent responsibility; integration and end-to-end tests provide evidence for connections and browser behavior.

lessonPractice.title: After changing a discount rule, which is best as a unit test?

options.label: Pass 99 and 100 to the discount function and assert no discount versus 20 off
options.feedback: Correct. It checks one clear rule with fixed input and expected output.

options.label: Submit 99 and 100 items through the order API, then check the discount in its response
options.feedback: This can find a problem, but it includes the API and order flow, so it is closer to an integration test.

options.label: Place 99 and 100 orders in the browser, then check the final amount on the confirmation page
options.feedback: That checks a complete result from the user entry point, which is closer to an end-to-end test and does not isolate the calculation.

data.agentPrompt: Add unit tests for the discount calculation: 99 gets no discount and 100 gets 20 off. Do not call real payment or network services; after the change, list both inputs and actual outputs.
